description: Velocx NZ is a performance swimwear retailer bringing elite global brands to New Zealand swimmers. Featuring Jaked, a premium Italian swimwear brand trusted by competitive athletes, Velocx helps swimmers train harder, race faster, and perform at their best.
tone: authoritative yet energetic, performance-driven, confident, aspirational, community-focused, athlete-first mindset

brand_positioning.velocx_role: trusted curator and performance authority in NZ swimwear
brand_positioning.jaked_positioning: elite Italian performance swimwear designed for competitive swimmers and race performance

target_audience.primary: competitive swimmers and triathletes in New Zealand aged 16–40
target_audience.secondary: fitness swimmers and aspiring athletes who want high-performance gear
target_audience.entry_level: younger swimmers or beginners influenced by elite athlete content
psychographics: wants to improve performance and times
inspired by elite athletes and competition
cares about quality gear and progression

content_pillars.details: tips, drills, technique breakdowns, race strategies
show Jaked in action, benefits, performance angles, not hard selling
adapt TikTok/IG trends into swimming niche

content_types.description: strong 1-3 second hook, problem or POV-based
show Jaked during training or racing naturally
explain why performance swimwear matters (without hard selling)

_note: Instagram and TikTok are in platforms config but credentials not yet configured. Update 'platforms' array and add credentials to config/credentials/velocx_nz.env when ready.

optimal_times: 03:00 NZST — retained as the primary posting slot from the previous strategy based on the confirmed top-performing post (engagement 4, image format) published at this exact hour in the prior analysis period; this signal is the strongest available engagement data point in the account history and must not be overridden by the current period's Facebook insights best_posting_hours (15:00, 13:00, 14:00) which reflect only zero-engagement posts published at 20:00 and carry no useful timing signal; 03:00 catches early morning swimmers pre-training and late-night scrollers; use for the highest-priority image post each week — specifically the undeployed six-beat kick stat post which combines every confirmed high-performance signal

23:00 NZST — retained as the secondary posting slot from the previous strategy based on the second-best performing post (engagement 2) published at 23:14 in the prior analysis period; evening wind-down browsing window for athletes post-training; use for secondary image posts including gear_closeup and lifestyle formats

21:00 NZST — retained as the tertiary posting slot based on the third and fourth ranked posts (engagement 1 each) published at 21:28 and 21:01 in the prior analysis period; consistent with post-training evening engagement window; use for supporting content when 03:00 and 23:00 slots are filled; note that the Facebook insights best_posting_hours (15:00, 13:00, 14:00) from the current period represent zero-engagement posts only and are not actionable timing signals — do not adopt afternoon scheduling
best_days: Sunday to Thursday — aligns with training day scroll behaviour in recovery windows; insufficient day-level variance in the archive to establish a statistically reliable day preference since all 31 posts were published at the same time with no day-level testing; low confidence on specific day ranking — review after 4 additional weeks of varied-day publishing at 23:00 and 03:00 to establish a day-level engagement signal; avoid Friday and Saturday as primary posting days until day-level data confirms or contradicts this assumption
top_content_types: race_action — highest-frequency image type in archive (2 of 6 image posts) and present in top-performing posts in the previous period; cinematic athlete mid-stroke butterfly or freestyle launching off blocks with water exploding around the body, race dive, underwater dolphin kick, finish wall touch, Jaked swim cap visible; confirmed by May 2026 trend research as the top-performing visual format in competitive swim social; prioritise as primary image type for at least one post per week; overhead and side-lighting compositions create strongest engagement signals in this category

gear_closeup — used only once in 31 archive posts yet confirmed by all five research briefs as the highest-traction format for performance swimwear brands in 2026; Jaked racing suit submerged in deep teal pool water with dramatic orange-amber overhead spotlights raking across fabric texture and compression panelling detail; post-nationals purchase-intent window confirmed still active through May per multiple research briefs; this format is severely underused relative to its recommended priority — increase to at least one dedicated post per week immediately; pair with compression science or hydrodynamics caption framing rather than pure product showcase

training — not yet used in archive despite being confirmed as a high-relevance seasonal format across all five research briefs; early morning empty indoor pool with single swimmer in lane, coach on deck, athlete drilling; autumn training block framing is the highest-relevance seasonal context for NZ competitive swimmers in May 2026; cinematic underwater view from directly below with crepuscular light rays from pool surface is the specific trending visual variant confirmed in April 2026 visual research and not yet deployed in the archive — treat as priority new format to test this period

lifestyle — not yet used in archive; athlete poolside post-session with towel over shoulders, focused intense expression, wet hair, warm amber stadium overhead lighting; autumn training mood resonates strongly with NZ swim audience in base-building phase per multiple research briefs; portrait composition with subject in upper 60% of frame per brand composition rules; pair with mindset or mental performance caption angle to maximise resonance in current season
top_pillars: Swim Performance and Training — stat-backed educational tip posts with specific data hooks are the highest-engagement and highest-saving content type in competitive swim social communities on Facebook and Instagram in 2026 per all five research briefs; undeployed high-priority angles remain from the previous strategy and have still not been published: six-beat kick (10.21% 50m improvement stat), hip rotation (10 degrees equals longer stroke and less drag), pull buoy dependency (masks broken body position and kills split times without the buoy), and hand entry and catch position (immediate drag from poor angle); each of these angles has a confirmed scroll-stopping stat hook ready to use; this pillar must anchor at least 2 image posts per week; bullet-structure drill breakdowns with a stat anchor in the first line are the save-driving format confirmed across all research briefs

Jaked Product Integration — post-nationals purchase-intent window confirmed still active through May by multiple research briefs; gear_closeup format used only once in 31 archive posts yet is the highest-recommended visual format for performance swimwear brands in 2026; suit compression science and hydrodynamics framing must lead all product content — pure product showcase without performance context is explicitly flagged as underperforming in all research briefs; increase to at least 1 dedicated image post per week using submerged suit or fabric detail cinematic photography; Italian performance fabric angle and compression fabric hydrodynamics framing are both confirmed high-relevance product content directions this period

Athlete Mindset and Motivation — sports psychology and mental performance content confirmed outperforming technique-only posts for competitive swim audiences in 2025–2026 per April 2026 research; taper mindset psychology and final 50m mental toughness angles are both confirmed undeployed and high-relevance; all mindset content must be anchored to a specific technique, time stat, or NZ swim season context to avoid the zero-engagement generic motivation format; post-nationals reflection and autumn base-building block framing are the specific NZ-relevant mental performance angles to use through May and June 2026

Trends and Viral Formats — Instagram photo carousel format gaining traction in niche sports communities per April and May 2026 research; five-frame drill breakdowns with a surprising stat on frame one are the confirmed high-save carousel structure; team swim challenge formats confirmed driving exponential sharing per April 2026 research; this pillar remains the most underutilised in the archive and represents the highest growth lever on Instagram and TikTok; test one carousel or trend-adapted post per week in addition to the standard three-post schedule

voice_guide.headline_style: short punchy, 2–5 words, imperative or bold statement
voice_guide.caption_style: hook first, story/value middle, soft CTA at end — no hashtags in body

image_style.description: Dark, moody, cinematic — professional sports/editorial photography quality
photography_style: dark moody cinematic — not bright or cheerful
rich deep blue/teal pool water as primary background colour
dramatic overhead or side lighting creating strong highlights and deep shadows
high contrast — subjects pop against dark surroundings
motion blur or frozen-motion water droplets add energy
shallow depth of field — subject sharp, background softly blurred
avoid: smiling lifestyle shots (we want focused, competitive, intense)
any competing brand logos on suits, caps, or equipment
composition_rules: bottom-centre area should be darker/less detailed — VelocX logo is overlaid there
leave breathing room — don't crowd every corner
portrait images: subject in upper 60%, pool/water fills lower portion
landscape images: subject left or centre, water/pool atmosphere right

color_palette.accent_lighting: warm orange-amber #F8A30E from stadium overhead spots
color_palette.athlete_skin: warm highlighted tones against dark water
color_palette.suit: sleek dark racing suit, no visible competing brand logos

image_style.prompt_base: dark cinematic indoor pool, dramatic orange-amber overhead spotlights, deep teal water, high contrast chiaroscuro lighting, professional sports photography, bottom area dark for text overlay

image_types.race_action: athlete mid-stroke (butterfly, breaststroke, freestyle), race dive off blocks, underwater dolphin kick, finish wall touch. Water exploding around the body. Jaked swim cap visible.
image_types.training: athlete drilling in lane, coach on deck, early morning empty pool with single swimmer, pull buoy, paddles
image_types.gear_closeup: sleek racing swimsuit flat lay on pool tiles or submerged in water, goggles with pool reflection, Jaked cap detail. Deep blue/teal water as backdrop.
image_types.lifestyle: athlete poolside post-session, towel around shoulders, focused expression, warm stadium lighting, wet hair
image_types.open_water: New Zealand coastal swim, ocean or harbour, dramatic sky, wetsuit or racing kit
image_types.team: swim club warm-up, lane full of swimmers, coach briefing athletes pre-race
